title: How to Test Ad Creatives on a Small Budget | AIVideosUGC
description: An ad creative is the video or photo in your ad. Test a few versions together from one photo, change one thing at a time, and read the results.
h1: How to Test Ad Creatives Without Guessing
lead: You learn which opening people actually watch, by changing one thing at a time. For a wall clock, that one thing might be the first second: the face at dawn, or a hand hanging it on tile. Run those files together.
secondary_keywords: ad creative testing for small business
summary: You find a winning opening without a second filming day. Change one thing, and run a few versions on the same audience and budget.

sections.h2: What Is a Video Ad You Can Test
paras: You pay to show a short clip of the lamp you ship, and you can open one file on the shade and another on a hand switching it on. Both start from the same photo.
The same rules keep the test fair. One difference between files, the same audience, and the same budget.

sections.h2: How to Compare Versions From One Product
paras: You can compare openings because the photo, the length, and the shape stay the same. Change only how the clip starts.

For a ceramic mug, one version can open on a counter, another on a desk, and a third as a wrapped gift. Photo ads work the same way, with the same mug and the same line. When the only change is the AI actor or the tone, ask for that and keep the mug. Build the still versions with the [AI ad image generator](page:social-ad-photos).

When the test is about who is in the frame, keep the coat photo and the first second, and change only the person. Keep the line the same in that file.
Each opening is its own file from the same clock, with no extra filming day.

You get a file back with the opening you named. Read the line, and keep the file when the clock in the picture is the clock you ship.

sections.h2: Benefits of Testing More Than One Ad
paras: The next version is another file you can make from the photo you already sent. Send it again and change one thing.
You can see the credit charge before you commit a filming day.
One headphones photo can feed an opening on the case and an opening on the ear. Keep the headphones the same, and keep the length the same in those two files.
When the same headphones ad has been in front of the same people for a while and they scroll past, retire that file. The next file changes the first second and keeps the price the same.
You decide what the line is allowed to claim. When the tea tin's page names the leaf, the line can name that leaf. The photo still has to show your tin.
You can use the download in ads and on your store. It has no watermark. The version that wins can run as a paid ad.

sections.h2: How Shops Set Up One Test
paras: Skincare. Three openings of the same bottle, and only the first second changes.
Home. One photo becomes a clip, and the room stays the room in the photo.
Gadgets. A hand holds the product in one version and sets it on a desk in the next.
Apparel. The presenter changes, and the garment color stays the color you photographed.
Food. The spoken language changes for a second market, and the dish stays the same.
Supplements. The script names only what is on the label.
Beauty. The presenter speaks a line the shop wrote.
Kitchen. One photo stands in for building a set, and the next opening is another file.
Pets. The product stays visible while the opening line changes.
A catalog. The same notes run across several products, then an API repeats that for new arrivals.

sections.h2: How to Keep a Small Test Fair
paras: Change only one thing between versions, so the result points at that one thing.
Worth testing, one at a time: the opening moment, the setting, the shape, the length, and the line you add afterward. Start with the opening. It decides whether anyone sees the rest.
sections.alt: Adult hands place the same plain round wall clock beside blank color cards.

sections.h2: How the Versions Should Run Together
paras: One campaign gives every version the same audience, the same budget, and the same product page.

Many ad accounts let several ads share one group. Some also offer a built-in test that shows each version to part of the audience. The account may spend more on one version early. A version that barely ran has not been tested. Leave the ads as they are while the test is live, so the account keeps counting the same test.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold the same plain round wall clock in two matched side-by-side positions.

sections.h2: How to Tell Which Version Works
paras: Wait several days, until each version has actually played, before you name a winner.

Read three numbers in order. First, how many people stay past the opening. That tells you if the start works. Second, how often people click. That tells you if they wanted to visit. Third, the cost each time someone buys, or adds the item to the cart. That matters most for the shop. A version can get more views and still lose on sales. If the numbers are close, that change did not matter much. Keep the one you prefer and test a bigger difference next.
sections.alt: Hands rest beside blank color cards and the same plain round wall clock.

sections.h2: What the Next Test Should Change
paras: You keep the version that brings sales at a cost you can accept, turn off the clear losers, and change one new thing.

Write down the date, what changed, and the result. After a few rounds you will see what your buyers respond to. When a winner starts costing more per sale, make fresh versions. Work through the opening, the setting, the shape, the length, then the offer. Each round starts from what already worked.

paras: A fair test uses one difference, a few versions, and the same audience and budget. Leave them as they are while they run.
Judge after several days, write down the result, and let the next round change only the next thing. Every file still shows the product you ship.

faq.q: What do people mean by a video ad generator?
faq.a: A way to get a short paid-ad file from a product you already sell. For a desk lamp, you bring the photo, and you name the first second. The crew stays off the calendar for that test.

faq.q: How do I create a video ad to test?
faq.a: Upload the backpack photo and write the first second you want, such as the zipper coming into view. Download the shape this test uses.

faq.q: What should I look for when I pick a tool for ad tests?
faq.a: You want a second opening of the same backpack without a new photo shoot. The useful tool is the one that can make that second opening.

faq.q: Do I pay to make each version?
faq.a: Yes. A clip is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark. It can run as a paid placement and sit on the product page. You can run it without a separate permission form.

faq.q: Which frames can I download, and where can they run?
faq.a: Use 9:16 when the test runs on a phone screen, 1:1 when it sits in a feed, and 16:9 when the screen is wide. 4:3 and 3:4 are only for a placement that lists them. A second shape is a different test.

faq.q: Can one test cover every candle in the catalog?
faq.a: Yes, if each candle has its own photo. Reuse one opening as the note, and let an API start a file when a new candle arrives. Forty candles means forty files.

faq.q: Should I stop filming with people I hire?
faq.a: No. Keep a filmed spot when you want a person you hired on camera. Use a generated file when you are still choosing the first second. They answer different questions.

faq.q: Can a generated ad be turned down by the ad account?
faq.a: It can, for the same reasons any ad can. If the line sounds like a customer wrote a review, say so the way that app currently asks you to. Rules change, so read them before you raise the budget.

faq.q: How many versions should a small shop run?
faq.a: Start with a few, often three. More than that splits a small budget so far that no version gets a fair chance to play. Every extra version is another file.
The opening. It decides whether anyone watches the rest. Keep the product, the length, and the shape the same until that result is clear.

faq.q: Can I change the price on only one version?
faq.a: No. While you are testing the video or the photo, put the same words, the same price, and the same music on every file. Test the offer in a later round, on its own.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: From the ad account, after each version has played. This page does not invent a winner. You read who stayed, who clicked, and what a sale cost.

faq.q: What if the ad account barely shows one version?
faq.a: That version was not tested. Wait until each file has had a real chance to play, or the comparison is noise.

faq.q: Do I have to say the presenter is generated?
faq.a: Yes, when the ad could be read as a real customer's review. Follow that platform's disclosure rule. Give the AI actor a name you chose for the shop.

cta_title: Test One Change at a Time
cta_lead: You see which opening people watch, from a few versions of one product photo. Keep everything else the same, and read that in your ad account.
